title: Send Money From the US Quickly by Scanning Your Recipient's Bank QR Code
summary: A landlord in Florianópolis texts you a Pix QR code and wants the deposit by Friday.
body_markdown:
A landlord in Florianópolis texts you a[Pix QR code](https://moretapay.com/networks/pix) and wants the deposit by Friday. You fund your Moreta Pay balance in dollars, scan the code, check the recipient name, exchange rate and amount that will arrive, then confirm. Done. Moreta Pay is a wallet connected to Brazil's Pix rail and national QR networks across Asia and Latin America, funded from your US bank or card. You can scan a recipient's personal bank QR code from that balance, so the recipient is paid in local currency on the rail they already use.


## How does sending money by scanning a bank QR code work?


The method rests on one idea: the recipient's bank writes the payment details, not you. A bank QR code is a machine-readable instruction. It holds the recipient's account identifier, their name and sometimes a fixed amount. Americans already use a domestic version: the Zelle QR code.


Cross border payments by QR add one step in the middle, which is a currency conversion. Many national systems also share a common format.


Think of the code as an envelope addressed by the recipient's own bank. You never copy the address by hand, which removes the risk of a wrong digit in an account or branch number during an international money transfer.


## Why can't a US banking app pay a foreign bank QR code?


The catch is that only the local postal service delivers that envelope. Pix,[DuitNow](https://moretapay.com/networks/duitnow) and[KHQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/khqr) are domestic instant-payment rails. They move money between institutions inside one country. Your US checking account isn't one of those institutions, so your banking app has nowhere to send the instruction.


Joining a rail directly requires local paperwork. A Brazilian bank account requires a CPF tax number, and local wallets typically ask for a local phone number or ID. This is the wall people hit when they try to send money abroad the way locals pay each other.


The gap closes with a wallet that holds your dollars and is itself connected to the local rail. Moreta Pay can send to a bank account, to another Moreta user, or to a local QR rail such as Pix.


## Which national QR rails might your recipient send you?


The rail behind a code tells you what your recipient will receive. These are the rails in markets where Moreta Pay works:

Check three limits before you promise anyone a payment:


- **China:**


Paying in China works only while you are physically there.[WeChat Pay](https://moretapay.com/networks/wechat-pay) is for trips, not for transfers from home.


- **Mexico:**


If you need to send money to Mexico, it isn't on Moreta's country list. A bank-account transfer service is the better route.


- **App availability:**


Availability depends on your country, payment method and app version.


## How do you send money from the US by scanning a QR code?


The procedure is the same whichever rail the code uses:


1. **Fund your balance.**


Link a US bank through Plaid and top up by ACH, or use a Visa, Mastercard, American Express or Discover card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. You can also fund with USDC or USDT on Solana, but crypto-funded money can't be spent in Cambodia or China.


2. **Scan the code.**


Choose send money and scan the recipient's QR code. If the code arrived as a screenshot on your phone, open it on a laptop and scan the screen.


3. **Check the review screen.**


It shows the fee, exchange rate, amount that arrives and expected delivery time.


4. **Confirm.**


Make sure the recipient name matches the person you meant to pay, then send.


Your balance stays in dollars until you pay. The conversion uses the rate shown on screen.


## How fast and how cheap is it compared with a bank transfer?


A transfer is only as fast as its slowest step, and with a QR transfer that is rarely the QR payment itself. Digital wallet and QR payments can often settle instantly, while traditional international bank transfers are much slower. Cost works the same way. The World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide report for Q3 2025 found that


[banks remain the most expensive channel for remittances, at an average cost of 14.99 percent](https://remittanceprices.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/2026-04/RPW_main_report_and_annex_Q325.pdf)


.

Here is how the fees add up on a 300 USD payment:


- **ACH funding:**


the top-up is free because it is over 250 USD, plus the 1.5% send fee, for 1.5% in total.


- **Card funding:**


the 2.5% top-up fee plus the 1.5% send fee comes to roughly 4% in total.


Free ACH funding is also the slowest route, so start it early. Moreta Pay also sets a maximum single payment and a weekly limit for each country. In Brazil, for example, that is 16,000 BRL per payment and 32,000 BRL per week.


## Where does a QR transfer fit among Wise alternatives?


Fees aside, the bigger choice is how the money is delivered. Comparisons of money transfer apps such as Wise and Revolut usually focus on account-to-account transfers, which assumes your recipient gave you an account number. Start with what they actually sent you:


- **An account number and bank code:**


use an account-based transfer service.


- **A Pix, DuitNow or KHQR code:**


use a wallet connected to that rail to pay it directly.


- **No bank app at all:**


no QR will reach an aunt selling num banh chok outside Siem Reap who only handles riel notes. Plan a cash route instead.


QR is the most direct way to pay people who are already on a national rail. It does nothing for people who aren't.


## Is it safe to pay a QR code someone sends you?


The QR code is only an instruction, so the real risk is paying the wrong person. Someone can swap a screenshot in a group chat. That makes the recipient name on the review screen the line to check. For a new landlord, send a small test amount first.


Moreta Pay safeguards:


- Every payment needs your confirmation in the app.


- Every account is identity-checked with a selfie and passport.


- Transactions are monitored around the clock.


- Funds are held by banking partners.


Transfers between Moreta users can't be refunded, so double-check those before you send.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can I pay a Pix QR code from my US banking app?


No. You need a wallet connected to Pix, funded from your US account.


### Do I need a bank account in the recipient's country?


No. You can pay local QR codes from your own bank, no local account needed.


### How long does a QR transfer from the US take?


Funding by ACH takes 1-3 business days. The review screen shows the expected delivery time before you send.


### What does it cost?


Moreta Pay charges 1.5% per payment. The fee and live rate are shown before you confirm, plus any top-up fee for your funding method.


### Can I fund with stablecoins?


Yes, with USDC or USDT on Solana. Crypto-funded balances can't be spent in Cambodia or China.


### What should I set up before my first transfer?


- Verify your identity, which usually takes a few minutes.


- Link your US bank through Plaid.


- Ask the recipient for their full name so you can match it on the review screen.
